name: Fort Hood (Cavazos)

image.alt: Fort Hood sign at Frank W. Mayborn Gate, June 24, 2025
image.credit: U.S. Army photo by Eric Franklin, Fort Hood Public Affairs (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: One of the largest Army installations in the world, home to III Armored Corps in Central Texas. Renamed Fort Cavazos in 2023 and Fort Hood again in 2025.

name: Joint Base San Antonio

image.alt: Quadrangle clock tower, JBSA-Fort Sam Houston (landmark, not a gate)
image.credit: Photo by Sean Worrell, 502d Air Base Wing (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: Military City USA: JBSA-Lackland, JBSA-Fort Sam Houston and JBSA-Randolph form one of the largest joint bases in the Department of Defense.

name: Fort Bliss

image.alt: Buffalo Soldier Gate, Fort Bliss, Aug. 20, 2021
image.credit: Photo by Staff Sgt. Michael West (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: A sprawling Army post in El Paso, Texas, home to the 1st Armored Division, with sunny weather and mountain views.

name: Fort Bragg

image.alt: Headquarters XVIII Airborne Corps and Fort Bragg sign, March 7, 2025
image.credit: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Alexcia Rupert, 22nd Mobile Public Affairs Detachment (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: Home of the Airborne and Special Operations forces in North Carolina. Renamed Fort Liberty in 2023 and Fort Bragg again in 2025.

name: Camp Lejeune

image.credit: Photo courtesy of U.S. Marine Corps (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune on the North Carolina coast, home of II Marine Expeditionary Force, with miles of beaches.

name: Joint Base Lewis-McChord

image.credit: Photo by Ingrid Barrentine, courtesy of the Northwest Guardian (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: A joint Army and Air Force installation south of Tacoma, Washington, between Puget Sound and Mount Rainier.

name: Fort Campbell

image.credit: U.S. Army photo by Sam Shore (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: Home of the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault), straddling the Kentucky-Tennessee line near Clarksville.

name: Naval Station Norfolk

image.alt: Aerial view of Naval Station Norfolk
image.credit: Photo by Petty Officer 2nd Class Christopher Stoltz, U.S. Navy (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: The world's largest naval station, in the heart of Hampton Roads, Virginia.

name: Camp Pendleton

image.alt: Marines at the Camp Pendleton main gate, Jan. 6, 2020
image.credit: U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Dylan Chagnon (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton stretches along 17 miles of Southern California coastline between Los Angeles and San Diego.

name: Fort Carson

image.alt: ID check at a Fort Carson gate, April 16, 2020
image.credit: U.S. Army photo by Pfc. Ashton Empty (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: The Mountain Post, at the foot of the Rockies just south of Colorado Springs, home to the 4th Infantry Division.

name: Fort Benning

image.alt: Leaders at the new 'Welcome to Fort Benning' sign, April 16, 2025
image.credit: Photo by Patrick Albright, Fort Benning Public Affairs Office (public domain, via www.dvidshub.net)

blurb: The home of the Infantry and Armor in west Georgia. Renamed Fort Moore in 2023 and Fort Benning again in 2025.
